clue.text: Cereal tart comes apart according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds of a phrase change places

blocks.note: a flan is an open tart
something that comes apart breaks
swap the opening FL and BR sounds

explanation.surface: A baker watches a pastry fall to pieces, with a breakfast cereal somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Say FLAN BREAKS with its first sounds exchanged and you get BRAN FLAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran flakes are a common breakfast cereal made from toasted wheat bran.

clue.text: Animated creature annoys insects

blocks.note: first meaning: the cartoon rabbit of Looney Tunes
second meaning: irritates or pesters
third meaning: small creepy-crawlies

explanation.surface: A cartoon character pesters some insects.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one short word: a cartoon name, a verb, and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugs Bunny is a cartoon rabbit; to bug someone is to irritate them; bugs is everyday slang for insects.

clue.text: Worker on current Taylor Swift tour accommodates old boy with actor

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one string of letters houses another inside it

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker
taken as written
I is the physics symbol for electric current
The Eras Tour was Taylor Swift's record-breaking concert tour
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
and means together with

explanation.surface: A roadie on Taylor Swift's tour finds room for an old schoolboy alongside a film star.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT, ON and I followed by ERAS make one long string, and that whole string takes OB AND into its middle; 'with' is wordplay, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Banderas is a Spanish film star known for The Mask of Zorro and Pain and Glory.

clue.text: Frenzied US agent arresting continually

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to hold them, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: a Fed is an FBI agent in American slang
ever means always, at all times

explanation.surface: A wild-eyed FBI officer keeps making arrests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arresting' sits naturally with an agent in the surface, but here it is the instruction to put one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Fevered describes excited, frantic activity, a close synonym of frenzied.

clue.text: Cooler song playing after number one in charts

indicators.note: the number one position of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song
the first letter of the word
something playing is on

explanation.surface: A chilled-out track is on air after a number one in the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one in charts' sounds like a chart-topper, but it means just the first letter of 'charts'; ON is placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircon is short for air conditioning, a machine that lowers room temperature, so it is a cooler.

clue.text: Tense amid raising certain vessel of ancient civilisation

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts its letters so they read bottom to top
amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: certain means sure
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a can is a container

explanation.surface: A tense moment while lifting a particular jar from an ancient culture.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal and container apply only to the first part; the vessel is simply added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were the people of ancient Etruria in Italy, so the adjective means belonging to that early civilisation.

clue.text: Sanction lab tests in prime locations

indicators.note: prime locations are positions numbered by prime numbers: second, third, fifth, seventh

blocks.note: letters 2, 3, 5 and 7 of the two words run together

explanation.surface: Laboratory testing is approved at the best sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime locations' sounds like estate-agent talk, but it means positions 2, 3, 5 and 7: A, B, E, T.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something can mean to support or permit it, and to abet is to encourage or assist.

clue.text: Arrest in depressed Black Sea area reduced type of offences

indicators.note: something reduced is cut down, so the last letter is lopped off

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling depressed
to collar someone is police slang for arresting them
Crimea is the peninsula jutting into the Black Sea

explanation.surface: Someone is detained in a gloomy part of the Black Sea region for minor crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: CRIMEA loses its final A to give CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-collar crime is a category of offending such as theft or vandalism, typically associated with manual workers.

clue.text: Corrupt state is out to get renegade priest

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled and altered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A corrupt government is being ousted, leaving room for a rogue cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates was the seventeenth-century English clergyman who invented the 'Popish Plot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oates was an ordained Anglican who dabbled with Catholicism and fabricated a conspiracy, so he fits a turncoat cleric.

clue.text: Shake off alien with short run outside

indicators.note: something short has been cut, so the word loses its last letter
to be outside something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to run a country is to govern it
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: Someone tries to escape an alien by sprinting a little way around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' here is govern, not sprint; trimmed to GOVER it goes around ET.
explanation.definitionFit: To get over an illness or setback is to recover from it, which is shaking it off.

clue.text: Trainee is bad smell source, reportedly

indicators.note: reported means passed on by word of mouth, so we go by what is heard

blocks.note: a reek is a bad smell and a root is a source

explanation.surface: The new trainee is blamed as the origin of a nasty odour.
explanation.walkthrough: REEK plus ROOT, spoken quickly, gives the pronunciation of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruit is a newly enlisted soldier or employee still learning the job.

clue.text: Fright to cycle causing concerns

indicators.note: to cycle is to go round, so the front letter moves round to the back

blocks.note: a scare is a fright

explanation.surface: Being frightened of cycling gives a person worries.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARE sends its S to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cares and concerns are both plural nouns for worries or anxieties.

clue.text: Parisian you introduced to knight, queen and king said to be worrying people

indicators.note: said means spoken, so we go by the sound rather than the spelling

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
vous is French for you
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is presented to royalty and a knight, who seem to be anxious types.
explanation.walkthrough: VOUS is joined to N and ER; REX spoken aloud supplies the spelling of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous wrecks are people in a state of acute anxiety, people who are worrying a great deal.

clue.text: Separatist is to replace English in plan

indicators.note: to replace means to take the place of, so one letter is swapped out for another

blocks.note: a schematic is a diagram or plan
E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: A breakaway figure aims to substitute something for English in a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: In SCHEMATIC, the E is swapped for IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A schismatic is someone who causes or joins a split from a church or group, a breakaway member.

clue.text: Dull chapter precedes resounding conclusion to story

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter
resounding means loud
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boring chapter comes before a story's big, noisy ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precedes' just places the chapter's C first in the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull weather is grey and overcast, which is what cloudy describes.

clue.text: Gold only gathered in middle of Somali tombs

indicators.note: the middle of something is its centre, so just the central letters are kept
to be gathered in is to be drawn into a fold, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the two central letters of the six
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: Gold alone was collected from the heart of Somali burial sites.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural is the Latin one rather than mausoleums, which the letter count rules out.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand building housing a tomb or tombs, so the Latin plural means tombs.

clue.text: Los Angeles detectives engaged in work calmly

indicators.note: to be engaged in something is to be occupied inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to ply a trade is to work at it
LA is the standard abbreviation for Los Angeles
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives

explanation.surface: Police detectives in LA go about their job with composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the verb to ply, as in plying a trade; CID is the British police's detective branch, an unexpected partner for Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and untroubled, so the adverb describes doing something calmly.

clue.text: Name of female special constable trained without fancy concepts

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a set of letters is taken out
something trained has been bent into a new shape, so the letters are reordered
fancy means elaborate and freely arranged, so the letters to remove can come in any order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A part-time police officer's name, someone trained to avoid fancy ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Take every letter of CONCEPTS out of SPECIAL CONSTABLE, leaving S, I, A, L, A, B, L, E, then rearrange those. A special constable is a British volunteer police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a girl's given name, so it is a name belonging to a woman.

clue.text: Ground near the harbours

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so the letters are concealed inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Land close to the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbours' paints a seaside scene, but it is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground and earth are both words for soil, or for the land underfoot.

clue.text: Maybe lament from one wanting tanning stick

definitions.text: Maybe lament from one wanting tanning

blocks.clueFragment: Maybe lament from one wanting tanning
blocks.note: first meaning: a complaint someone hoping for a suntan might voice about their skin, split as two words
second meaning: to pierce or run through with a spike

explanation.surface: A sunbather moans about their complexion while holding a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as I'M PALE and it is the complaint of someone wanting a tan; 'maybe' signals it is just one example of such a lament.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale something is to pierce it with a sharp point, as you stick meat on a skewer.

clue.text: Neglect when leader’s abandoned job

indicators.note: the leader is the opening letter, and abandoning it means dropping it

blocks.note: an omission is a failure to do something, a neglect

explanation.surface: Negligence follows when a boss walks away from their post.
explanation.walkthrough: OMISSION loses its first letter, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is an assigned task or operation, so it is a job someone is sent to do.

clue.text: Oddly knew this hard task might be unworkable

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the letters are shuffled together into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; this is the result of the mix, so letters come out of it
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone strangely sensed that this tough job could not be done.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards: KNEW mixed with 'this' (the answer) might be UNWORKABLE. Take K, N, E, W out of UNWORKABLE and the remaining U, O, R, A, B, L rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour means physical toil or hard work, so a demanding piece of work is labour.

clue.text: Declaims, with scorn, about recent “masterpiece”

indicators.note: about can mean all around, in no fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic sneeringly holds forth about a new work that others call a masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around masterpiece suit the critic's sneer, and also hint the answer is a label rather than a verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern classic is a recently made book, film or album already regarded as one of the greats.

clue.text: Kid heard river

indicators.note: heard means received by ear, so we want a word that sounds the same

blocks.note: to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A child listened to a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning to joke with. The Tees is a river in north-east England, flowing out at Middlesbrough.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a major river of north-east England, so it is an example of a river.

clue.text: Rubbish around front of cottage that man had burnt

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters read backwards
the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
the opening letter of the word
he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: A man had set fire to the junk piled around his cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it puts rubbish round the cottage's letter, but it turns the rubbish about instead; the apostrophe of he'd is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To torch something is to set it on fire deliberately, so torched means burnt.

clue.text: Around four gold mines completely stripped rock-forming mineral

indicators.note: stripping a word strips its outer layers, leaving just its inside letters
around means encircling, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: the inner letters once the outer two go
the inner letters once the outer two go
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Roughly four gold mines have been fully exhausted of a mineral found in rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'gold' and 'mines' lose their outer letters, and together they go round IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivine is a green silicate mineral that is a major component of basalt and the Earth's mantle.

clue.text: Seashore bar originally outrageous project

indicators.note: bar means except or excluding, so a letter is left out
originally points to the origin, the first letter

blocks.note: the coast is the seashore
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A beachfront bar was originally a scandalous scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' wants to be a pub on the beach; it means except. COAST without O.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something is to throw or fling it forward, and to cast is to throw.

clue.text: Keeps covering yard with field plants

indicators.note: to cover something is to go over and around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to keep is to have
yd is the abbreviation for yard
a range is an area or field, as in a field of vision or range of vision

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a garden yard and a field covered in shrubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' is the verb to have, conjugated; 'field' is an area of scope, as in a range of interests.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrangeas are flowering garden shrubs with large rounded heads of blooms.
